And you must try, for a test, To bathe in these three big cauldrons, In the milk and in the two waters.”

speaker: IVAN
text: “See where he is going with this!”

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Ivan began to say.

speaker: IVAN
text: “They scald only piglets, And turkeys, and chickens; Look, I am not a piglet, Not a turkey, not a chicken. Now, in cold water, I might Bathe all right, But when you begin to warm it, You will not tempt me. Enough, Tsar, of your cunning and cleverness, And of seeing Ivan off!”

speaker: NARRATOR
text: The Tsar, shaking his beard:

speaker: TSAR
text: “What? Am I to bargain with you!”

speaker: NARRATOR
text: He cried.

speaker: TSAR
text: “But look! If at the break of dawn You do not do what I order, I will give you over to torment, I will have you tortured, And torn into little pieces. Out of here, you plague!”

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Then Ivan, weeping, Dragged himself to the hayloft, Where his little horse lay.

speaker: KONEK
text: “What is the matter, Ivan dear? Why do you hang your head? I think our old bridegroom Has thought up a new trick?”

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Said the little horse. Ivan fell on the little horse's neck, Hugged him and kissed him.

speaker: IVAN
text: “Oh, it is trouble, little horse!” he said. “The Tsar is getting rid of me for good; Think, he orders me To bathe in cauldrons, In milk and in two waters: One cold water, In another boiled water, And the milk, you know, boiling.”

speaker: NARRATOR
text: The little horse said:

speaker: KONEK
text: “Now that is a real service! Here all my friendship is needed. I must say, by the way: We had better not have taken the feather; From that villain feather So much trouble has come on your neck... Well, do not cry, God be with you! We will manage this trouble somehow. I would sooner die myself Than leave you, Ivan. Listen: tomorrow at dawn, When, in the courtyard, You have undressed as you should, Say to the Tsar: ‘Could you not, Your Grace, order My Humpbacked Horse to be sent to me, To say goodbye to him for the last time.’ The Tsar will agree to it. Then, when I wave my tail, Dip my nose into the cauldrons, Spray you twice, And whistle a loud whistle, Be sure you do not yawn: Dive first into the milk, Then into the cauldron of boiled water, And from there into the cold. And now say your prayers And go quietly to bed.”

speaker: NARRATOR
text: The next day, early in the morning, The little horse woke Ivan:

speaker: KONEK
text: “Hey, master, enough of sleeping! It is time to do your service.”

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Then Ivan scratched himself, Stretched, and got up, Said a prayer to the fence, And went to the Tsar's courtyard.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: There the cauldrons were already boiling; Beside them, in a row, sat The coachmen, and the cooks, And the servants of the court, Zealously adding wood, Talking about Ivan Quietly among themselves, And laughing now and then.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Then the doors opened; The Tsar and the queen appeared And got ready from the porch To look at the brave fellow.

speaker: TSAR
text: “Well, Ivan, undress, And bathe in the cauldrons, brother!”

speaker: NARRATOR
text: The Tsar cried to Ivan. Then Ivan took off his clothes, Not answering a word. And the young queen, Not to see his nakedness, Wrapped herself in her veil. Ivan went up to the cauldrons, Looked in, and scratched himself.

speaker: TSAR
text: “Why have you stopped, Ivan?”

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Cried the Tsar again.

speaker: TSAR
text: “Do what you must, brother!”

speaker: IVAN
text: “Could you not, your Grace, Order my Humpbacked Horse to be sent to me? I would say goodbye to him for the last time.”

speaker: NARRATOR
text: The Tsar, thinking, agreed And ordered The horse to be sent to him. The servant brought the little horse And stepped aside himself.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Then the little horse waved his tail, Dipped his nose in the cauldrons, Sprayed Ivan twice, And whistled a loud whistle. Ivan looked at the little horse And dived into the cauldron at once, Then into another, and then into the third, And became so handsome That no tale can tell And no pen can write! Then he put on his clothes, Bowed to the Tsar-Maiden, Looked about him, in good heart, With a grand air, like a prince.

speaker: CROWD
text: “What a wonder!”

speaker: NARRATOR
text: They all cried.

speaker: CROWD
text: “We never heard of it, That one could grow handsomer!”

speaker: NARRATOR
text: The Tsar ordered himself undressed, Crossed himself twice, Splash! into the cauldron, and was boiled there!

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Then the Tsar-Maiden stands up, Gives a sign for silence, Lifts her veil, And speaks to the servants:

speaker: MAIDEN
text: “The Tsar has ordered you to live long! I want to be your queen. Do you like me? Answer me! If you like me, then acknowledge As master of everything And as my husband...”

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Then the queen was silent, And pointed to Ivan.

speaker: CROWD
text: “We like you, we like you!”

speaker: NARRATOR
text: They all cry.

speaker: CROWD
text: “For you we would go even to the end of the world! For the sake of your good fortune We acknowledge Tsar Ivan!”

speaker: NARRATOR
text: The Tsar takes the queen, Leads her to God's church, And with his young bride He walks round the altar.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: The cannon fire from the fortress; The forged trumpets blow; They open all the cellars, They set out barrels of foreign wine, And the people, having drunk, Shout with all their might:

speaker: CROWD
text: “Hail to our Tsar and Tsaritsa! To the most beautiful Tsar-Maiden!”

speaker: NARRATOR
text: And in the palace the feast is a mountain: Wine flows like a river, At oak tables The nobles and princes drink. It is a joy to the heart! I was there, I drank mead, wine and beer; It ran down my moustache, But not a drop got into my mouth.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: And that is the end of the tale. Thank you for listening, and sleep well.
